projects.story:
## The need

Valaippadu is a fishing village in Poonakary, about 50 km west of Kilinochchi. Most families here depend on fishing for their living. Valaippadu RCTM School serves this community. Because of today's economic difficulties, parents cannot bear the extra cost of special uniforms for the school's prefects, like the ones prefects wear in urban schools.

## The plan

The school's newly appointed principal has taken several commendable steps to raise its educational standards and improve its buildings and facilities. Special uniforms for the prefects would strengthen discipline, leadership, responsibility and the students' confidence, and give rural students the same opportunities as students in town.

The request asks for about **Rs 150,000** for special uniforms for the prefect students (25 to 50 students), to support the school's continued development. It will also take an extra cost off families during difficult times.

## The impact it will make

Between 25 and 50 student prefects at Valaippadu RCTM School will wear special uniforms, just like prefects in urban schools. The uniforms will strengthen discipline and leadership in the school, help the prefects take on responsibility with confidence, and give rural students an equal opportunity. Families facing hard times are spared an extra cost, and the new principal's work to lift the school's standards gets real support.

*Everything the requester wrote is on this page.*

projects.title: Pussellawa kids' trip to Hanuman Kovil
projects.summary: The children of Pussellawa spent a day at Hanuman Kovil: running and playing on the lawn, dancing together and looking out over the hills, with transport and food fully covered.
projects.quote: The children truly enjoyed the experience and were very happy.
projects.story:
## Summary

The children of Pussellawa spent a day at Hanuman Kovil, in the hills on the road between Gampola and Nuwara Eliya. They ran and played on the lawn, danced together in their best clothes, shared a meal and looked out over the mountains.

## The need

Pussellawa is a tea-country town, and many of its children grow up among the estates. Families work hard and a day away together is rare. Transport and food are what stand between these children and a day out.

## The day

On 12 October 2026 a hired vehicle took the children to Hanuman Kovil. On the big lawn they played running games, held hands in circles and danced, while the grown-ups watched over them. Some of the little ones simply stood and looked out at the mountains.

The local organisers wrote to us the same day: *"The children truly enjoyed the experience and were very happy."*

## Where the money went

Every rupee went to the day itself: Rs 10,500 for the vehicle and Rs 8,750 for food, Rs 19,250 in total.

## What it leaves behind

A day of joy the children will remember, and the first Raavanaa day in the hill country. Thank you to everyone who made it possible.

projects.title: Yogapuram pre-school trip to the Black Bridge

budget.item: The day out for the pre-school children

projects.summary: Seventeen little ones from a pre-school in Yogapuram went by bus to the old Black Bridge over the Pali Aru and to Banalingeswaram temple at Oddankulam: ice cream, dancing, playing in the river and a day to remember.
projects.quote: The happiness on the children's faces is the greatest gift we received.
projects.story:
## Summary

On 12 October 2026, 17 children from a pre-school in Yogapuram, with 20 parents, two teachers and members of the management, went on a trip to the Black Bridge (Karutha Palam) over the Pali Aru and to the Banalingeswaram Narmatha Natheeswarar temple, both at Oddankulam.

## The need

The pre-school is run by a local community centre, and 25 children study there. Before the trip, the manager wrote to us: *"For many of these children a day like this comes rarely. It will be a day to remember, to play, to laugh and to eat together."*

## The day

The bus left the pre-school at 3.30 in the afternoon and reached the Black Bridge at 3.45. The old bridge, said to have been built by the Dutch, crosses the Pali Aru. The children had ice cream, danced together, watched the river flowing quietly under the bridge and then went down into the water to play. For many of them it was the first day like this in a long time.

Next they visited Banalingeswaram temple, where they looked at the carved sculptures of the 64 Nayanmars and walked through the flower garden. Outside the temple they danced again and shared snacks. Everyone left at 5.45 and was back at the pre-school by 6.00.

The day after, the manager wrote: *"It was a wonderful day! The happiness on the children's faces is the greatest gift we received. Our heartfelt thanks to Raavanaa and to everyone who helped make this day possible."*

## Where the money went

The full cost of the trip, Rs 20,000.00, was covered: the bus, food and snacks, and what the children needed for the day.

## What it leaves behind

A happy afternoon by the river for the whole pre-school, and photos and videos for the families to keep. Thank you to everyone who made it possible.

projects.story:
## Summary

A day at the sea for about 25 children: sand, waves, kites and a good lunch under the casuarina trees at Karainagar.

## The need

Many of these children live less than an hour from the sea and have never spent a day on the beach. Transport, food and a safe group are what stand between them and the shore.

## The plan

A van takes the group to Casuarina Beach in the morning. The children play games, fly kites and build sandcastles with volunteers watching the water, then share lunch in the shade before heading home with a small gift.

The project is **activated**: it is fully funded by Kiri & Family, the place is visited and the van is booked. We are now getting the volunteers ready.

## What it leaves behind

A first day at the sea that the children will remember. After the trip we will share the story and the pictures here.

projects.story:
## Summary

A day out for mums and their children together: games, a shared lunch and time to simply enjoy each other.

## The need

The mums we work with carry their families alone or nearly alone. Days off are rare, and days out with their children rarer still.

## The day

A bus took the families out for the day. The children and their mums played games side by side, shared a big lunch and finished with a family photo for each mum to keep.

This project is **complete**. It was made possible by Sasi, Shanker and Bala.

## What it left behind

Mums who laughed with their children all day, and a photo on the wall to remember it by.

## Summary

We are planning a trip to the arcade for children from an orphanage: games, lights, prizes and a day made just for them.

## The need

Children growing up in a home rarely get a day that is only about fun. A few hours of games and little prizes is a small thing to give and a big thing to receive.

## The plan

An afternoon at the arcade where the only thing the children have to do is play, with transport, food and helpers arranged for the group.

The project has been **initiated**. We are waiting for the budget and the other details of the trip. As soon as they are ready, they will be shown on this page.

## What it leaves behind

A day the children will talk about for a long time. After the trip we will share the story and the pictures here, so that everyone who gave can see the smiles they created.

projects.story:
## Summary

The pupils of a small Tamil primary school in Pussellawa have never been on a school trip. On 27 November 2026 they hope to spend a day in Kandy, at the Temple of the Tooth and the Peradeniya Botanical Gardens.

## The need

The school has 52 children and 6 teachers in a hard-working tea-country community. The principal calls it a fully disadvantaged school, and says these children have never been anywhere on an excursion. She and her teachers decided together to give them a new experience, and asked Raavanaa for help after our first day in Pussellawa in October.

The school's sign sets out what it is for. Its vision is to give society primary pupils with sound skills and good character. Its mission is to give every pupil all the core skills and the chance to go on to secondary education.

## The plan

On Friday 27 November 2026, about 55 children and teachers travel by bus from the school to Kandy, about 50 km away. They visit the Sri Dalada Maligawa, the Temple of the Tooth, and stop at the Peradeniya gardens on the way back. The school has permission for the trip from the Department of Education.

The whole day costs Rs 61,000: about Rs 30,000 for the bus and the rest for food for the whole group.

## What it leaves behind

A first school trip the children will remember. After the day, the organiser will send photos and videos, and we will share the story and the pictures here, so that everyone who gave can see the smiles they created.
